incidents.victim: Oracle E-Business Suite users (payments processing)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of a critical flaw (CVE-2026-46817, CVSS 9.8) in the EBS payments module, with early exploitation attempts observed from a single IP against ~950 internet-exposed instances.
incidents.impact: Early-stage exploitation of exposed EBS systems (over half in the US); researchers warn of a possible mass-exploitation wave echoing the 2025 Clop EBS extortion campaign.

incidents.victim: Microsoft 365 users (finance, HR, logistics staff; US life-sciences firm targeted)
incidents.vector: Device-code OAuth phishing kit (ARToken/EvilTokens) that bypasses MFA and steals Primary Refresh Tokens, paired with vendor-impersonation emails aimed at accounts-payable staff.
incidents.impact: Credential and token theft enabling persistent mailbox and SharePoint access that survives password resets, used for business email compromise fraud.

incidents.victim: Aflac Japan
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the customer portal and internal systems (method undisclosed).
incidents.impact: Personal data of ~4.38 million policyholders exposed and bank/premium-payment details of ~230,000 customers compromised; Japanese systems affected, US operations unaffected.

incidents.victim: Oracle PeopleSoft customers (Nissan North America confirmed)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of an Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day vulnerability.
incidents.impact: Data breach at Nissan North America amid a broader PeopleSoft zero-day hacking spree hitting multiple organizations.

incidents.victim: European and Asian hotels and accommodation providers
incidents.vector: Guest-impersonation phishing with malicious LNK-in-ZIP files and PowerShell chains deploying a Node.js implant and a blockchain-C2 RAT (TONResolver).
incidents.impact: Long-term persistent access to hotel systems with evidence of credential theft; blockchain dead-drop C2 hampers takedowns.

incidents.victim: US Department of Homeland Security (Homeland Security Information Network)
incidents.vector: Compromise of HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: Intrusion into the network used to share sensitive information with federal, state, local and industry partners; scope of stolen data still unknown.

incidents.victim: Central Bank of Libya
incidents.vector: Network breach and data exfiltration by the Qilin ransomware group.
incidents.impact: Stolen files leaked on the dark web; the intrusion was traced to about three weeks before disclosure and is under investigation.

incidents.victim: Tata Electronics (Apple and Tesla component data)
incidents.vector: Breach and exfiltration of 200,000+ documents by the World Leaks group.
incidents.impact: Leaked documents expose Apple and Tesla component designs (including iPhone 18 parts, battery specs and chips); the company refused the ransom.

incidents.victim: ~140,000 malware-infected computers worldwide
incidents.vector: Modular malware — Amadey for initial access paired with StealC for credential and data theft.
incidents.impact: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit disrupted the infrastructure behind large-scale credential theft that fed ransomware and fraud; operators observed rebuilding.

incidents.victim: Polymarket (prediction market platform)
incidents.vector: Third-party vendor compromise leading to malicious code injected on the Polymarket website.
incidents.impact: About $3 million stolen from users; the company detected and contained the incident and is reimbursing affected users.

incidents.victim: District of Columbia Housing Authority
incidents.vector: Cyberattack disrupting the housing authority's IT systems.
incidents.impact: Website and email servers disrupted; voucher and housing payment processing continued with restoration underway.

incidents.victim: Government officials, military personnel, journalists and activists (Ukraine, Europe, US)
incidents.vector: Phishing impersonating commercial messaging-app support to trick targets into surrendering backup recovery keys and verification codes.
incidents.impact: Account takeovers exposing historical and ongoing private and group messages; tracked by the FBI as UNC5792 and UNC4221 activity.

incidents.victim: Southeast Asian critical infrastructure (electricity, water, government, military)
incidents.vector: Exploitation and lateral movement deploying a novel C# backdoor (TinyRCT) with anti-analysis features.
incidents.impact: More than 10 organizations compromised, including a vulnerable water utility; limited data exfiltration observed, assessed as pre-positioning for follow-on operations.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government/military and entities tied to Italian foreign policy
incidents.vector: Multi-component .NET backdoor (STOCKSTAY) using WebSocket command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Persistent espionage access enabling file exfiltration, command execution and screen capture; part of continuous tooling development since 2022.

incidents.victim: Communications service provider (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager)
incidents.vector: Rogue SD-WAN peering plus chained zero-days (CVE-2026-20127/20182 auth bypass, CVE-2026-20245 privilege escalation).
incidents.impact: Root-level access to the centralized SD-WAN Manager, creating potential to intercept enterprise traffic across branch sites; remediated with Mandiant.

incidents.victim: KDDI email systems (STNet, JCOM, Chubu Telecom, NIFTY, BIGLOBE)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in third-party software used by KDDI's email platform.
incidents.impact: Unauthorized access exposing customer email addresses and passwords across KDDI and five partner ISPs; intrusion blocked on detection.

incidents.victim: Nidec (Chaun Choung Technology, Taiwan subsidiary)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion and ransomware deployment by the BlackField group.
incidents.impact: About 2TB of corporate data (HR, financial, procurement, manufacturing, legal, IT) stolen and a $2 million ransom demanded; the subsidiary's isolated network limited spread.

incidents.victim: Belgian State Security Service (Sûreté de l'État)
incidents.vector: Compromise of an Ivanti EPMM mobile-device-management platform operated by a third-party contractor.
incidents.impact: Names, phone numbers and email addresses of Belgian intelligence officials stolen; linked to prior-year exploitation of Ivanti EPMM servers.

incidents.victim: Japan Self-Defense Forces
incidents.vector: Malware-infected USB drives connected to classified networks.
incidents.impact: Infected drives reached classified systems; it is unclear whether data was stolen, the incident was undisclosed for about a year, and NATO partners are being notified.

incidents.victim: 18,000+ online stores using the Okendo Reviews widget
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of the Okendo Reviews widget injecting ClickFix JavaScript that lures shoppers into running malicious commands.
incidents.impact: Infostealers and remote-access trojans pushed to visitors across 18,000+ storefronts; the malicious code was removed on May 14, 2026.

incidents.victim: SecondFi (cryptocurrency platform)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a bug in the platform's web-wallet generation software.
incidents.impact: More than $2.4 million in customer assets stolen; the platform entered maintenance mode and pledged to refund affected users.

incidents.victim: Transport for London, UK retailers (M&S, Co-op, Harrods) and US healthcare (SSM Health, Sutter Health)
incidents.vector: Help-desk social engineering and SMS phishing to bypass MFA and gain network access (Scattered Spider).
incidents.impact: Members pleaded guilty or were charged over ransomware and extortion attacks that disrupted transit and major retailers and hit US health systems, with ransom demands up to $8 million.

incidents.victim: Klue and ~20 downstream customers (LastPass, Huntress, Recorded Future, Snyk, Jamf, Tanium, Gong and others)
incidents.vector: Compromise of business-intelligence vendor Klue via a legacy integration credential, then stolen OAuth tokens used to raid connected Salesforce instances.
incidents.impact: Salesforce data (financial information and PII) stolen from 20+ security and tech firms; the attacker (Icarus, tied to ShinyHunters) is extorting Klue and downstream victims.

incidents.victim: Fortinet FortiGate / SSL VPN operators (global)
incidents.vector: Mass credential brute-forcing (~1.16B attempts), SSL VPN hash interception with GPU cracking, and exported-config abuse across ~74,000 FortiGate devices in 194 countries ("FortiBleed").
incidents.impact: Administrative and VPN credentials compromised across critical-infrastructure and enterprise networks, including confirmed exfiltration of classified documents from a Turkish NATO contractor; credentials resold to other actors.

incidents.victim: Consumers via counterfeit Android TV boxes (1.4M+ IP addresses)
incidents.vector: Malicious Popa SDK preinstalled on Android TV boxes, enrolling home networks into a residential proxy service without meaningful consent.
incidents.impact: More than 1.4 million device IPs abused for ad fraud, account takeovers and data scraping; infrastructure tied to NetNut/Alarum Technologies.

incidents.victim: Conti ransomware victims (law-enforcement action)
incidents.vector: Wire-fraud conspiracy tied to Conti ransomware operations.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty after extradition from Ireland for his role in Conti ransomware attacks.

incidents.victim: National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack on NAIC systems attributed to ShinyHunters.
incidents.impact: The insurance standards database was compromised; risk designations were suspended and data-sharing with credit agencies halted before the attackers were evicted and operations restored.

incidents.victim: Fox Rothschild (law firm)
incidents.vector: Network breach by the Silent Ransom Group.
incidents.impact: Firm data was stolen and a ransom demanded; the firm reportedly refused to pay.

incidents.victim: Sapporo Holdings subsidiaries (Pokka Singapore, Sleeman Breweries Canada)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion with suspicious activity detected (method undisclosed).
incidents.impact: Suspected unauthorized access under investigation for possible data theft; domestic Japanese operations were unaffected.
